column1: # chunking-rules.tsv — how a spec's text is cut into clause-level units.
# Read by BOTH the Python builder (3gpp embedings/build_clause_index.py) and the
# Java service, so the rules exist in exactly one place. Nothing about chunking
# is compiled in; adding a spec family with different conventions is a new row.
# ── WHY THE PATTERNS ARE NOT LINE-ANCHORED ───────────────────────────────────
# Newlines did not survive ingestion: 0 of 200 sampled chunks in 36.331, 36.322,
# 38.331 and 23.501 contain a single "\n". Every "^"-anchored rule would match
# nothing. All patterns below are therefore INLINE and must carry their own
# left-context guard.
#   split <TAB> priority <TAB> name <TAB> regex
#       A match STARTS a new unit. The unit runs to the next split point or to
#       max_chars. Capture group 1, when present, names the unit (the IE name).
#   marker <TAB> priority <TAB> name <TAB> regex
#       Records a region label on units that fall inside it; does not itself cut.
#   limit <TAB> - <TAB> key <TAB> value
# Lower priority number wins when two rules match at the same offset.
# max_chars is 1200 on purpose: the cross-encoder's window is ~1382 characters
# (max-length 384 tokens). Measured before this change, 99% of chunks in the LTE
# RAN specs exceeded that window, so their tail was invisible to reranking — the
# permitted values of an IE sat past the cut and could never be scored. Staying
# under the window removes that failure by construction rather than by tuning.
# ── ASN.1 information-element definitions: the highest-value boundary ─────────
# "maxRetxThreshold ENUMERATED {t1, t2, ... t32}" is what decides a compliance
# question, and it is unambiguous inline. 36.331 contains 3754 of these, 38.331
# 3575 — each becomes its own unit instead of one line inside a 3000-char block.
split
# ── ASN.1 region markers: label units, do not cut ─────────────────────────────
marker
marker
marker
# ── Clause headings, for specs with no ASN.1 (36.322, 23.501, 28.552 ...) ─────
# Inline and therefore risky: "see clause 5.2.1 Transmit operations" must NOT cut.
# The negative lookbehind excludes the words that introduce a CROSS-REFERENCE
# rather than a heading. Lower priority than ie_definition so an ASN.1 spec is
# always cut on IEs first.
split
limit
limit
limit
